record.original_question: For binary black-hole systems, can one determine gravitational-wave emission and waveform predictions with sufficient precision for optimal signal detection and parameter extraction in gravitational-wave astronomy?

evidence.quote: Problem CMP2: Determine the predictions of emitted waveforms for binary black hole systems for optimal detection and parameter extraction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In general relativity, a binary black-hole system consists of two black holes inspiraling under mutual gravitational attraction, eventually merging and ringing down to a single Kerr black hole. The system radiates gravitational waves whose two polarization time series h_+(t) and h_×(t) (the gravitational-wave strain) depend on the intrinsic parameters (component masses m_1, m_2, spin vectors S_1, S_2, eccentricity e, etc.) and extrinsic parameters (sky location, distance, inclination, polarization angle, time and phase of coalescence).

For a gravitational-wave detector (such as a kilometer-scale interferometer) with one-sided noise power spectral density S_n(f), the standard noise-weighted inner product on signal space is
   ⟨a|b⟩ = 4 Re ∫_0^∞ ã(f) b̃*(f) / S_n(f) df,
and the match between two waveforms is the inner product of their normalized versions, maximized over time and phase shifts. A waveform family h_model(λ) is said to be sufficiently accurate for detection if its mismatch with the true signal h_true(λ) satisfies 1 − match(h_model, h_true) ≲ 1/(2 ρ²) where ρ is the signal-to-noise ratio, and sufficiently accurate for parameter estimation if the systematic bias it induces on each parameter λ_i is smaller than the corresponding statistical uncertainty σ_i for the relevant detector network and SNR regime.

Problem. Provide a theoretical/numerical prescription that, given any point λ in the physically relevant parameter space of binary black holes (including arbitrary mass ratio, arbitrary precessing spins, eccentricity, and the full inspiral–merger–ringdown), produces gravitational-wave waveform predictions h_+(t; λ), h_×(t; λ) that meet both the detection-accuracy and parameter-estimation-accuracy criteria above for current and next-generation gravitational-wave observatories, and quantifies and controls the modeling error throughout this parameter space.
artifact.category_tag: Gravitational waveforms from binary black holes
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is actively being addressed but remains open in full generality. Effective-one-body, phenomenological, and numerical-relativity surrogate waveform models cover much of the quasi-circular aligned-spin and precessing parameter space, and have been used successfully in LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA observing runs. However, recent work (2023–2026) shows that waveform-model systematics remain a leading concern: regions of high mass ratio, strong precession, eccentricity, and high SNR still exhibit biases exceeding statistical uncertainties, motivating ongoing development of eccentric numerical-relativity surrogates, accuracy-aware Bayesian inference, and improved precessing models. The general goal of waveforms accurate enough across the entire parameter space for next-generation detectors is not yet achieved.

status_evidence.title: Incorporation of model accuracy in gravitational wave Bayesian inference
status_evidence.snippet: Inclusion of model mismatch information in gravitational wave parameter estimation improves on current model-averaging methods, allowing higher-accuracy inferences.
status_evidence.claim: Waveform-model inaccuracies remain a recognized limitation in current parameter estimation, with new methods proposed to mitigate them.

status_evidence.title: Eccentric binary black holes: A new framework for numerical relativity waveform surrogates
status_evidence.snippet: New numerical-relativity surrogate framework for eccentric binary black holes.
status_evidence.claim: Eccentric BBH waveform modeling is still under active development as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: Mitigating Systematic Errors in Parameter Estimation of Binary Black Hole Mergers
status_evidence.snippet: Systematic effects include inaccuracies in waveform models in some regions of parameter space; as detector sensitivity improves, waveform models need to catch up.
status_evidence.claim: Waveform-model systematics remain a known limitation, especially as detector sensitivity grows.

status_evidence.title: Accurate and Efficient Waveform Model for Precessing Binary Black Holes
status_evidence.snippet: New precessing waveform model designed for accuracy and efficiency.
status_evidence.claim: Precessing-spin waveform modeling continues to be refined.
